title: Next-Word Machines
about: How a chatbot builds an answer one likely word at a time.

cards.prompt: Like your phone's keyboard, a chatbot guesses what usually comes next. Which word is it **most likely** to pick?
cards.context: I'm so hungry, I could eat a
cards.hint: Is it choosing what's sensible to eat, or what people often write?
cards.nudge: That's sensible to eat, but it isn't choosing food. Which ending do people say most?
cards.explanation: "I could eat a **horse**" is a common saying, so it turns up in text far more than any snack. The model picks what usually comes next, not what makes sense.

cards.title: Guessing the next word
cards.body: A chatbot is built on a **language model**. Having read huge amounts of text, it reads everything so far and gives each possible next word a **chance**: after "The cat sat on the", "mat" 60%, "sofa" 20%, "moon" 5%. It picks one, adds it, and repeats.

cards.prompt: Order the steps a chatbot repeats for each word. Once added, a word stays put.

items.label: Read all the text so far
Give each possible next word a chance
Add it to the end of the text

cards.hint: It needs the text before the chances, and the chances before it can pick.
cards.nudge: Start with what the model needs first: the text so far.
cards.explanation: **Read** the text, give each next word a **chance**, **pick** one and **add** it, then repeat with the longer text. (Really it uses word-pieces, but words are close enough.)

cards.prompt: The text has changed, with more words before it. Which word is **most likely** next now?
cards.context: Strapped in for launch, the cat sat in its
cards.hint: The loop reads **all** the text so far. Which words at the start change things?
cards.nudge: It reads everything, including "Strapped in for launch". What do you sit in on a rocket?
cards.explanation: The model reads **all** the text, so "Strapped in for launch" lifts **seat** to the top and drops "mat". Earlier words can change the next word.

cards.prompt: After "The cat sat on the", the model happens to pick "moon". What happens next?

options.text: "moon" stays, and it works out the next word from there
It sees "moon" was unlikely and swaps it for "mat"
options.nudge: Look at the loop: read, chance, pick, add. Does any step go back?

options.text: It ignores "moon" and carries on from "sat on the"
options.nudge: Step one reads **all** the text so far. What's in it now?

options.text: It stops, because an unlikely word means it went wrong
options.nudge: The model doesn't judge its own picks. It just keeps going round the loop.

cards.hint: Follow the loop once more: after "moon" is added, what does it read?
cards.explanation: The loop never goes back: the next chances come from "The cat sat on the moon". One odd pick can steer everything after it.

cards.prompt: After "Fish and", "chips" has a **70%** chance: 70 in 100 tries. In **10** tries, how many "chips" would you expect?
cards.hint: 70 out of every 100 is the same share as how many out of every 10?
cards.nudge: A chance isn't "always". 70 in 100 is the same share as 7 in 10.
cards.explanation: **7** out of 10: the same share as 70 in 100. A chance is "how often", not "always": the other 3 times it picks something else, like "peas".

cards.prompt: A chatbot writes "The Eiffel Tower is in Paris". How did it come up with that?

options.text: It looked it up on a map before it answered you
options.nudge: A language model on its own doesn't look things up. What did it learn from?

options.text: It understands where places are, like a person does
options.nudge: It doesn't understand places. How does it choose each word?

options.text: It checked the fact was true before writing it
options.nudge: It doesn't check facts. Each word is a guess at what usually comes next.

options.text: Those words often appear together in text it read

cards.hint: Think back to how it picks every word.
cards.explanation: "Eiffel Tower" and "Paris" appear together in lots of text, so "Paris" gets a high chance. It's right because the pattern was common, not because it checked (though some apps can also search the web).

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- A **language model** gives each possible next word a chance.
- It picks one, adds it, and repeats until it's done.
- Likely isn't the same as checked or true.

Next: the setting that decides how adventurous its picks are.
